WF-03 Steps 0.5 + 1 combined (registry lookup + diagnose) for docs/issues/ISS-0721.yaml on branch feature/WF03-ISS0721-20260919 (already checked out and pushed). ORCH has already independently verified the following, in this same session, before dispatching this run at all -- confirm them yourself rather than re-investigating blind, but state in your result that you did confirm rather than just trusting this dispatch (HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.1): (1) `grep -n 'seed!(' lib/letflow/entities/event_types.ex` shows `Letflow.Entities.EventTypes.seed!/1` defined at line 117; (2) a repo-wide grep for `EventTypes.seed!` call sites (`grep -rn 'EventTypes\.seed!' .`) returns only test fixtures/design docs/the issue file itself -- zero lib/letflow/ production call sites; (3) `Letflow.TenantProvisioning.maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2` (tenant_provisioning.ex ~line 1074-1084) is the ISS-0072 precedent for the ENGINE's own event types, wired into `replay_migrations/2` at ~line 390 via `with :ok <- maybe_seed_platform_event_types(using_default_manifest?, tenant_id) do`; there is no equivalent call to Entities.EventTypes.seed!/1 anywhere in that with-chain or elsewhere in tenant_provisioning.ex.

Step 0.5: search docs/issues/*.yaml for status: resolved entries with similar symptoms (event-type registration gaps in tenant provisioning) -- ISS-0072 itself is the obvious match; cite it and note whether this is a recurrence of the SAME root cause (it is not -- ISS-0072 fixed the engine's own seed list, this is a structurally identical but functionally separate seed list for entity-record event types that was simply never wired at all) or a genuinely new instance of the same class of gap.

Step 1: produce a root-cause diagnosis (not just symptom restatement) naming exactly what a fix needs to change: which function needs a new call site, what the call shape should look like (mirroring maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2's pattern: idempotent-on-duplicate, {:error, {:event_type_seed_failed, reason}} on real failure, gated the same way -- note EventTypes.seed!/1 takes a `prefix` argument, not a tenant_id, so check its @spec/signature at event_types.ex:116 and state exactly what argument the new call site must pass and where that value is available in tenant_provisioning.ex's existing scope). Do NOT implement the fix. Do NOT write to docs/issues/ISS-0721.yaml yet (that is Step 5, after the fix is proven).
acceptance_criteria: Reproduces or directly confirms the described 500/:unknown_event_type failure mode by reading the actual code paths (Letflow.EventStore.Registry.validate_payload/3 and its rejection on an unregistered event type), not by trusting the issue's prose alone
Names the exact function and file where the new call site belongs, and the exact value flowing into EventTypes.seed!/1's prefix argument
States whether this is a recurrence of ISS-0072's root cause or a distinct instance of the same class (with reasoning)
Does not implement the fix -- routes to CODE-DESIGNER

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 -- REGISTRY LOOKUP: docs/issues/ISS-0072.yaml (status: resolved) is the matching prior entry -- same symptom class (a production write path 500s with the Registry.validate_payload/3 unknown-event-type rejection because no code path ever calls Registry.register_type/2 for that event type before the tenant's first real write). VERDICT: NOT a recurrence of the same root cause. ISS-0072's fix (commit eb69dd7) extended TenantProvisioning.maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2's @platform_event_type_seed_attrs list to cover the ENGINE's five write-path event types (TASK_COMPLETED, INSTANCE_CANCELLED, INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND, SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED, EXECUTION_ERROR) -- that list still only feeds Registry.register_type/2 directly and has no entry, and no mechanism, for the three ENTITY_RECORD_* event types. ISS-0721 is a distinct, never-wired seed list (Letflow.Entities.EventTypes.seed!/1, REQ-228, shipped separately from ISS-0072's own fix and with its own idempotent wrapper around Registry.register_type/2) that was simply never given a production call site at all -- a new instance of the same CLASS of gap (a seed list existing but uncalled outside tests), not the same underlying defect reappearing.

STEP 1 -- DIAGNOSIS (confirmed by direct code reading, not from the issue's prose):

Reproduction path confirmed by reading the actual code (not trusted from the issue report): Letflow.EventStore.Registry.get_type/2 (lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex:175-189) queries the tenant-schema-prefixed `event_type_registry` table for a row named `event_type`, and explicitly returns `{:error, :unknown_event_type}` (line 184) when Repo.one/2 returns nil -- 'never nil, never a raised exception' per its own @doc. validate_payload/3 (line 144-161) calls get_type/2 at line 150 and propagates that error tuple straight through at lines 157-158 with no rescue. Since ENTITY_RECORD_CREATED/UPDATED/DELETED rows are only ever inserted by Letflow.Entities.EventTypes.seed!/1 (event_types.ex:117-140, via Registry.register_type/2), and nothing in production code calls seed!/1, a freshly-provisioned tenant's schema has zero rows for those three event names -- so the first POST /entities/:type write, which flows through Letflow.EventStore.append_multi/3 -> Registry.validate_payload/3 (per lib/letflow/entities/records.ex:18-21's own moduledoc statement of this exact dependency), hits :unknown_event_type and 500s, exactly as ISS-0721 describes.

ORCH's three pre-dispatch facts independently re-confirmed, not trusted blind: (1) `grep -n 'seed!(' lib/letflow/entities/event_types.ex` -- @spec at line 116, def seed!(prefix) at line 117, matches. (2) repo-wide `grep -rn 'EventTypes\.seed!' .` -- re-run just now: every match outside event_types.ex itself is either a test file (test/letflow/**, test/mix/**, test/support/exam_fixtures.ex -- 22 files, all invoking it directly for their own setup) or a design/moduledoc reference (lib/letflow/design/req228-*.md, lib/letflow/design/iss0580-*.md, lib/letflow/entities/records.ex:20 -- read directly, confirmed it is prose citing seed!/1 in a moduledoc paragraph, not a call site) or docs/issues/ISS-0690.yaml and ISS-0721.yaml (the issue records themselves). Zero lib/letflow/ production call sites. (3) maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2 (tenant_provisioning.ex:1074-1084) read directly and confirmed as the ISS-0072 precedent, wired into replay_migrations/2 at line 390 (`with :ok <- maybe_seed_platform_event_types(using_default_manifest?, tenant_id) do`) -- confirmed no equivalent call to Entities.EventTypes.seed!/1 exists in that with-chain or anywhere else in tenant_provisioning.ex (the only lib/letflow/ hits for 'EventTypes.seed!' are zero, per (2)).

EXACT CALL-SITE LOCATION: Letflow.TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/2, lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex, inside the `with` chain at line 390 (currently `with :ok <- maybe_seed_platform_event_types(using_default_manifest?, tenant_id) do {:ok, applied_versions} end`). This is the same site maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2 is already wired into -- it runs once per replay_migrations/2 call, after Ecto.Migrator.run/4 has applied the tenant's DDL and after mark_migrations_applied/1, gated the same way (using_default_manifest? -- true only when the caller did not pass a custom migration_source, matching ISS-0072's own gating semantics so a caller supplying a partial/custom migration list does not get an entity-event seed attempt against a schema that might not even have the event_type_registry table's dependent DDL applied yet).

EXACT prefix ARGUMENT VALUE for EventTypes.seed!/1, and where it comes from: `schema_name`, already bound in replay_migrations/2's own lexical scope by the `%Registration{schema_name: schema_name} ->` clause at line 376 -- the SAME schema_name already passed as replay_migrations/2's own `prefix: schema_name` option to Ecto.Migrator.run/4 at line 384, and the same schema_name maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2's sibling call at line 390 does NOT need (it takes tenant_id instead, because Registry.register_type/2 -- called by maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2 directly -- takes tenant_id, not a schema-name prefix). By contrast, EventTypes.seed!/1's own @spec (event_types.ex:116) takes `prefix :: String.t()`, not a tenant_id, and its body (line 118) immediately calls `TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix)` to convert the schema-name string back to a tenant_id before calling Registry.register_type/2 itself -- confirmed by reading tenant_id_for_schema_name/1's own @doc (tenant_provisioning.ex:222-239): it is stated to be the deterministic reverse of schema_name_for_tenant/1, so passing replay_migrations/2's own `schema_name` variable as seed!/1's `prefix` argument round-trips correctly back to the same tenant_id already in scope. This matches the pattern every one of the 22 test call sites already uses -- every single one passes a schema_name/schema variable (e.g. `EventTypes.seed!(fixture.schema_name)`, `EventTypes.seed!(tenant.schema_name)`, `EventTypes.seed!(schema_name)`), never a tenant_id, confirming `schema_name` is the correct and only argument shape seed!/1 accepts.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE (for CODE-DESIGNER, not implemented here): add a new private function in tenant_provisioning.ex mirroring maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2's exact shape -- e.g. `maybe_seed_entity_event_types(using_default_manifest?, schema_name)` -- that calls `Letflow.Entities.EventTypes.seed!(schema_name)` and normalizes its return: seed!/1 already returns `{:ok, seed_result()}` on success (never bare :ok, unlike Registry.register_type/2's own {:ok, event_type} that maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2 discards) and `{:error, reason}` on real failure (seed!/1 already treats {:error, :duplicate_event_type_version} as idempotent-skip internally, per its own @doc at event_types.ex:106-114, so the wrapper does not need to special-case that error atom the way maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2 does for register_type/2's raw return). The wrapper should convert `{:ok, _}` to `:ok` and `{:error, reason}` to `{:error, {:event_type_seed_failed, reason}}` to match maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2's own error tagging convention, then be added to replay_migrations/2's with-chain at line 390 alongside the existing maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2 call, gated by the same using_default_manifest? flag, passing `schema_name` (not tenant_id) as its second argument.
